newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says east may have to wait until 2002.
newsitem.headline: EU says east may have to wait until 2002.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday negotiations with applicant countries from central and eastern Europe would be long and hard and they were unlikely to win European Union membership before 2002.

"Taking into account the possible duration of negotiations and time needed for ratification, the earliest realistic date for the first accessions is likely to be no earlier than 2002," the Commission said in a fact sheet on the EU's enlargement process.

The statement differed openly from recent statements from French President Jacques Chirac, a champion of enlargement into former communist Europe, that the leading candidates could be in the European club by the turn of century.
The Commission, spelling out clearly what many insiders have said privately for months, also said that it was unlikely the new members would be able to join the bloc at the same time.
Poland, Hungary, and the Czech republic, the most economically advanced, have lobbied hard to get in on their own merits and not wait for countries like Bulgaria and Romania to catch up.

The Commission is currently working on individual advice on each of the 10 eastern European countries which have applied to join the EU. It is also due to start talks with Cyprus while Malta's application to join has been put on hold.
It confirmed, following recent doubts over the timing of its advice, that it would make it available immediately after the end of ther EU's inter-governmental conference review of its treaties.
